wizened

WIZ-uhnd · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Wizened is shriveled or wrinkled with age.

The wizened old sailor had spent sixty years squinting into salt spray and sun.

Example

The wizened apple at the bottom of the fruit bowl had been forgotten for so long it had shrunk to half its size.

Wizened describes something, usually a person's face or hands, or an object like fruit, that has visibly shrunk and wrinkled with age.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shriveled: Shriveled means shrunk and wrinkled, and it can happen fast -- a grape shrivels in days, a balloon shrivels as the air leaks out. Wizened is shriveling earned slowly: a wizened face carries decades in its creases. Anything wizened is shriveled, but only long age makes something wizened.

withered: Withered means dried up, shrunken, and drained of life or strength -- a withered plant droops and cannot recover. Wizened shares the dryness and the wrinkles but not the weakness: a wizened elder can still be sharp and spry. Withered points to lost vitality; wizened only tells you how age looks.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

youthful: having the fresh qualities of youth

plump: full and rounded

Where it sits · how dried and shrunken it is — aged → wizened → mummified

aged vs. wizened: Something aged has simply grown old, and may look perfectly smooth; wizened is much further along the drying scale -- the years have visibly shrunk and creased it.

mummified vs. wizened: Something mummified has dried and shrunk far more completely than something merely wizened.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — wizen

root — wizen: to dry up, to shrivel (Old English (wisnian))

suffix — -ed

suffix — -ed: having the quality of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: wizen ("to dry up") + -ed = having dried up and shriveled.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: The Old English verb wisnian, 'to dry up,' faded out of the language long ago, leaving wizened with no other common English word built on its root. Only the ending -ed, 'having the quality of,' is a piece you will recognize elsewhere.

Word Building

Word Choice

Wizened is a concrete, physical word -- it describes how a face, hand, or piece of fruit actually looks after years of age or dryness, unlike "ossified" or "hidebound," which describe a rigid attitude or structure rather than a physical appearance.
